messages:
oncall-bot: INCIDENT PAGE: SEV-2 - customer 'omega-corp' reporting failed PrivateLink connections to our west-us service endpoint. Pager: @emma.g, @sanjay.k. Link to incident: https://incident.redwood.internal/INC-2026-0923

oncall-bot: Automated checks show increasing TCP resets and BGP path churn between us-west-2 and us-east-1 transit for prefixes announced by cust-omega (AS64530).

emma.g: Acked. picking this up. grabbing basic info from the topology map.

emma.g: Customer says traffic to the PrivateLink endpoint times out intermittently, around every 30s, then recovers. They see RSTs from our side.

amelia (customer-alerts-bot): Noted: cust-omega reported 2026-04-07T14:22Z first failure. Current impact: RPCs to authentication service failing for ~10% of requests.

emma.g: Running quick traceroute to the endpoint from our healthchecker container:
```
traceroute -n -w 1 -q 1 10.200.12.45
 1 10.0.0.1 1.2 ms
 2 198.51.100.5 3.4 ms
 3 203.0.113.9 45.6 ms
 4 * * *
```
Looks like packets drop after the transit exchange.

sanjay.k: I'm pulling BGP session flaps. Observed updates: multiple AS path changes for cust-omega prefixes, alternate paths via eqx-ix and aws-ix. BGP logs: 
```
Apr 07 14:21:12 bgpd: UPDATE from 203.0.113.9: withdrawn 10.200.0.0/16
Apr 07 14:21:13 bgpd: UPDATE from 203.0.113.9: announced 10.200.0.0/16 via AS64530,AS2914
Apr 07 14:21:42 bgpd: UPDATE from 203.0.113.9: AS path changed -> AS64530,AS3356
```
Suspect route oscillation at the interconnect level.

alex.r: I opened a ticket with the cloud provider NOC (AWS NOC) referencing IIDX-4521 and included BGP dumps + pcap. They replied asking for flow logs and time ranges.

maria.s: Meanwhile, we've got a mitigation option: fail traffic for cust-omega over their dedicated VPN tunnel (they have an active IPsec backup) and route around the PrivateLink path while the direct peering stabilizes. We can toggle the route advertisement to prefer the VPN next-hop.

emma.g: Can we do that safely? Any TLS termination implications?

maria.s: VPN preserves end-to-end. It's slightly higher latency but will keep control-plane traffic intact. Steps: 1) create a route override for cust-omega prefix in our edge router to prefer VPN next-hop 2) reduce Local Pref on flapping path to discourage selection.

opsbot: RUNBOOK ACTION: "Failover PrivateLink -> VPN" requested by @maria.s. Confirm with on-call before applying. Use: `infractl route set-preference --prefix 10.200.0.0/16 --next-hop 198.51.101.2 --local-pref 200`

emma.g: Sanjay — handoff to you in 15 if this still oscillating. If we do the route override, notify customer and our SREs.

sanjay.k: I can take. Oncall handoff: @emma.g -> @sanjay.k at 14:30Z. I'm joining the AWS NOC call now. ETA for route change: ~3 min to propagate.

tim.o: FYI finance/CS flagged this as customer-impacting; cust-omega is on Dedicated contract. Please log impact window for postmortem.

sanjay.k: Applying route override now:
```
# infractl exec on-edge --
infractl route set-preference --prefix 10.200.0.0/16 --next-hop 198.51.101.2 --local-pref 200
```
spawning change, will monitor.

sanjay.k: Change applied. Polling healthchecks and packet captures.

emma.g: Customer confirms reduced errors on their side — error rate dropped from 10% to 0.5% in the last minute. :thumbsup:

opsbot: NOTE: rollback plan prepped. Command to revert: `infractl route revert --change-id CHG-5819`

sanjay.k: Leaving the route override in place while AWS investigates the interconnect. Asked AWS NOC for a root cause timeline. They've escalated to network engineering.

aws-noc (via alex.r): AWS NOC: We see flaps at the peering fabric between eqx and our exchange, causing short path changes for the announce. We're evaluating a config rollback on the IX side. No ETA yet.

maria.s: Recording impact notes: Affected service: auth-api on PrivateLink endpoint. Customer impact: intermittent auth failures for ~14 mins before mitigation, ~2% requests failed during window. Next actions: keep VPN path active, coordinate with AWS, capture additional pcaps for postmortem.

emma.g: Good job team. Sanjay, please own the incident for the next 2 hours and coordinate final resolution and RCA. I'll write initial incident record.

sanjay.k: Acknowledged. I'll update the incident page and ping customer success for the SLA hit calculation.

oncall-bot: Handoff recorded: primary owner sanjay.k, secondary owner emma.g. Case closed when BGP stabilizes for 30m and route override removed.

maria.s: Also capturing a quick mitigation playbook snippet to add to runbook: "If PrivateLink flaps due to interconnect BGP churn, prefer encrypted VPN as fallback and notify provider NOC immediately."

tim.o: Noted for billing/SLA. Please attach time-series graphs and request id samples when you update the incident.

sanjay.k: Will attach tcpdump + BGP logs + timing. Scheduling post-incident review for tomorrow 10:00Z.

emma.g: Thanks everyone. Closing the page in slack — continuing coordination on the incident doc.

opsbot: REMINDER: update the incident tracker with impact classifications within 24h.
